QF.id: Issue Management - General Obligations and Due Diligence_40

question.text: What happens to the lock-in when a pledge on locked-in securities is invoked by the lender?

answer.text: The lock-in continues to apply; the transferee (lender) cannot further transfer until the lock-in expires
The lock-in is automatically released upon invocation of the pledge
The lock-in period is reset and starts afresh from the date of pledge invocation
SEBI must approve the transfer and may grant a new lock-in period

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the SEBI rule, when a pledge on locked-in securities is invoked, the lock-in continues to apply, and the transferee cannot transfer the specified securities further until the lock-in period expires. The lock-in attaches to the securities, not to the holder, so a change in ownership through pledge invocation does not extinguish or reset the period. The Trap: 'Lock-in is automatically released' is the intuitive but wrong answer. Resetting the lock-in or requiring fresh SEBI approval are not supported by the source. Note: Confirm with the lender that the continuing lock-in is reflected in their internal records before invocation so the transferee restriction is correctly tracked.
